03-01.t: Dr. Clara Swain Begins Formal Medical Training for Indian Women in Bareilly
03-01.s: Dr. Clara Swain started instructing 14 native Indian women in anatomy, physiology, and materia medica in Bareilly, resulting in 13 graduates receiving practice certificates in 1873.
Swiss physician and bacteriologist Alexandre Yersin, who discovered the bacterium responsible for bubonic plague (Yersinia pestis), died on this day.

03-01.t: Death of Nobel Laureate Georges J. F. Köhler
03-01.s: German biologist Georges J. F. Köhler, who shared the 1984 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for developing the technique to produce monoclonal antibodies, passed away.

03-02.t: Death of Anatomist Samuel Thomas von Sömmerring
03-02.s: German physician and anatomist Samuel Thomas von Sömmerring, best known for discovering the macula lutea of the human eye responsible for sharp central vision, died in 1830.

03-03.s: American biochemist Arthur Kornberg was born on this day; he won the 1959 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering the biological synthesis of DNA.

03-03.t: Death of Polio Vaccine Pioneer Albert Sabin
03-03.s: Albert Sabin, developer of the oral polio vaccine that broke poliovirus transmission and enabled global eradication efforts, died in Washington, D.C.

03-04.t: Birth of Smallpox Vaccine Pioneer Benjamin Waterhouse
03-04.s: Benjamin Waterhouse, co-founder of Harvard Medical School and the first physician to test and introduce the smallpox vaccine in the United States, was born.

03-04.t: Birth of Thoracic Surgeon Norman Bethune
03-04.s: Canadian thoracic surgeon and early universal health care advocate Henry Norman Bethune, renowned for frontline trauma surgery, was born.

03-05.t: Birth of APHA Co-Founder Elisha Harris
03-05.s: American physician and sanitary science pioneer Elisha Harris, principal founder of the American Public Health Association (APHA), was born.

03-05.t: Danish Cohort Study Confirms MMR Vaccine Does Not Cause Autism
03-05.s: A landmark nationwide cohort study of over 650,000 children in Denmark was released, providing definitive evidence that the MMR vaccine does not increase autism risk.

03-06.s: German pharmaceutical company Bayer registered Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) as a trademark, launching one of the most widely used medications in medical history.

03-06.t: Birth of mRNA Vaccine Scientist Özlem Türeci
03-06.s: German physician-scientist Özlem Türeci, co-founder of BioNTech and co-creator of the first approved mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine, was born.

03-07.s: American biologist David Baltimore was born; he won the 1975 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine at age 37 for discovering reverse transcriptase.
American geneticist Michael Rosbash was born; he shared the 2017 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for elucidating molecular mechanisms of circadian rhythms.

03-08.s: English physician John Fothergill, credited as the first to name and identify trigeminal neuralgia, was born on this day.

03-08.t: Birth of Cortisone Pioneer Edward Calvin Kendall
03-08.s: American chemist Edward Calvin Kendall was born; he shared the 1950 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his discoveries on adrenal cortex hormones.

03-09.s: English physician and geneticist David Weatherall, renowned for his foundational research on thalassemias and hemoglobinopathies, was born.

03-09.t: First Scribner Shunt Implanted for Chronic Hemodialysis
03-09.s: Dr. Belding Scribner implanted the first arteriovenous shunt in a patient, making long-term, repeated hemodialysis possible for kidney failure.

03-10.t: Death of Orthopaedic Surgeon Jacques Calvé
03-10.s: French orthopaedic surgeon Jacques Calvé, who co-described Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease in 1910, died on this day.

03-10.t: Death of Burn Care Pioneer Charles Rufus Baxter
03-10.s: American surgeon Charles Rufus Baxter, who introduced the Parkland formula for fluid resuscitation in burn patients in 1968, passed away.

03-10.t: Passing of Dr. R. Marthanda Varma, Founder Director of NIMHANS
03-10.s: Pioneering Indian neurosurgeon R. Marthanda Varma, the founder director of the National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences (NIMHANS) in Bengaluru, passed away at age 92.

03-11.t: Dr. Anandi Gopal Joshi Graduates with an M.D. in the United States
03-11.s: At age 21, Anandi Gopal Joshi graduated with a medical degree from the Woman's Medical College of Pennsylvania with a thesis on 'Obstetrics among the Aryan Hindus,' becoming the first Indian woman certified in Western medicine.

03-11.t: Birth of Dr. V. Shanta, Pioneering Indian Oncologist
03-11.s: Dr. Viswanathan Shanta was born in Mylapore, Chennai. She dedicated over six decades to the Adyar Cancer Institute, transforming it into a premier center for free and subsidized cancer care.

03-11.t: Death of Penicillin Discoverer Alexander Fleming
03-11.s: Scottish bacteriologist Sir Alexander Fleming, who discovered penicillin in 1928 and shared the 1945 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, died in London.

03-11.t: WHO Declares COVID-19 a Global Pandemic
03-11.s: The World Health Organization officially declared the novel coronavirus (COVID-19) outbreak a global pandemic, triggering worldwide public health responses.

03-12.t: Birth of Hepatitis B Vaccine Researcher Wolf Szmuness
03-12.s: Polish-born epidemiologist Wolf Szmuness, who designed and conducted the first clinical trials proving the effectiveness of a hepatitis B vaccine, was born.

03-12.t: Death of Pathologist Eugene Lindsay Opie
03-12.s: American physician and pathologist Eugene Lindsay Opie, who conducted pivotal research on tuberculosis transmission, diagnosis, and immunization, died.

03-12.t: India Confirms Its First COVID-19 Fatality
03-12.s: Health authorities in Karnataka and the Union Health Ministry confirmed India's first COVID-19 death involving a 76-year-old man from Kalaburagi who had recently returned from Saudi Arabia.

03-13.t: Birth of Neurosurgeon Alfred Washington Adson
03-13.s: American neurosurgeon Alfred Washington Adson, a pioneer of neurological surgery at the Mayo Clinic and namesake of Adson's sign and maneuver, was born.
American physician and psychiatrist Charles Krauthammer, who contributed to the creation of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders III (DSM-III), was born.

03-14.t: Birth of Chemotherapy Pioneer Paul Ehrlich
03-14.s: German physician and scientist Paul Ehrlich was born; his laboratory discovered arsphenamine (Salvarsan) for syphilis, initiating modern chemotherapy.

03-14.t: First Successful Penicillin Treatment in the United States
03-14.s: Penicillin was used for the first time in the United States to successfully treat a patient, ushering in the clinical antibiotic era.

03-15.t: Birth of Epidemiology Pioneer John Snow
03-15.s: English physician John Snow, a pioneer of anesthesia, medical hygiene, and modern epidemiology, was born on this day.

03-15.t: Birth of Diphtheria Antitoxin Discoverer Emil von Behring
03-15.s: German physiologist Emil von Behring was born; he won the inaugural 1901 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering a diphtheria antitoxin.

03-15.t: Birth of Waldemar Haffkine, Cholera and Plague Vaccine Pioneer
03-15.s: Bacteriologist Waldemar Mordecai Wolff Haffkine was born in Odessa. Working extensively in India from 1893 onward, he developed and deployed the first effective vaccines against cholera and bubonic plague.

03-16.t: Birth of Pioneering Physician Rebecca Cole
03-16.s: American physician and social reformer Rebecca Cole, the second African-American woman to become a doctor in the United States, was born.

03-16.t: Birth of MRI Inventor Raymond Vahan Damadian
03-16.s: Armenian-American physician and inventor Raymond Vahan Damadian, who invented the first magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanning machine, was born.

03-16.t: First Dose of Oral Polio Vaccine Administered Under Pulse Polio
03-16.s: India administered its first dose of the Oral Polio Vaccine under the Pulse Polio Immunisation Programme, a date now commemorated annually across the country as National Vaccination Day.

03-16.t: India Expands COVID-19 Vaccination to Ages 12-14 with Corbevax
03-16.s: India launched COVID-19 immunization for children aged 12-14 years using the Hyderabad-based Biological E's indigenous Corbevax vaccine, alongside precautionary doses for all citizens aged 60 and above.

03-17.t: Birth of Neurophysiologist Walter Rudolf Hess
03-17.s: Swiss physiologist Walter Rudolf Hess was born; he shared the 1949 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for mapping brain regions controlling internal organs.

03-17.t: Foundation Stone Laid for Lady Hardinge Medical College
03-17.s: Lady Hardinge laid the foundation stone of Lady Hardinge Medical College in New Delhi, establishing a dedicated institution to train women physicians in India.

03-18.s: Japanese physician and bacteriologist Ryukichi Inada, who discovered the pathogen responsible for Weil's disease (leptospirosis), was born.

03-19.t: Birth of Thoracic Surgeon Evarts Ambrose Graham
03-19.s: American physician and surgeon Evarts Ambrose Graham, renowned for performing the first successful pneumonectomy for lung cancer, was born.

03-20.t: Birth of Enzyme Kinetics Pioneer Maud Lenora Menten
03-20.s: Canadian scientist Maud Lenora Menten was born; she co-developed the Michaelis-Menten hypothesis explaining the velocity and mechanism of enzyme-catalyzed reactions.

03-20.t: Passing of Dr. Biresh Chandra Guha, Father of Modern Biochemistry in India
03-20.s: Indian biochemist Biresh Chandra Guha died at age 57. He established biochemistry as an independent academic discipline in India and made key contributions to vitamin, nutrition, and food science research, including during the 1943 Bengal famine.

03-20.t: Death of Nobel Laureate J. Michael Bishop
03-20.s: American immunologist and microbiologist J. Michael Bishop, who shared the 1989 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering the cellular origin of retroviral oncogenes, died in San Francisco.

03-21.t: Birth of DNA Sequencing Pioneer Walter Gilbert
03-21.s: American biochemist and physicist Walter Gilbert, an early supporter of human genome sequencing and the first to purify a gene regulatory protein, was born.

03-22.t: First Administration of Ether Anaesthesia in India
03-22.s: Just five months after William Morton's Boston demonstration, ether anaesthesia was administered for the first time in India at Medical College Hospital, Calcutta, under the supervision of Dr. R. O'Shaughnessy.

03-22.t: Birth of Pediatric Cardiac Surgeon Willis J. Potts
03-22.s: American pediatric surgeon Willis John Potts was born; he introduced the Potts shunt for blue baby syndrome and performed the first successful pulmonary artery sling repair.
American physician and epidemiologist Arnold Monto, whose research focuses on the prevention and treatment of viral respiratory tract infections, was born.

03-23.s: Swiss-born Italian pharmacologist Daniel Bovet was born; he won the 1957 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering drugs that block specific neurotransmitters.

03-24.t: Birth of Dame Edith Mary Brown, Founder of CMC Ludhiana
03-24.s: Medical missionary Dame Edith Mary Brown was born. In 1894, she founded the North India School of Medicine for Christian Women in Ludhiana, now Christian Medical College (CMC), Ludhiana, Asia's first medical school for women.

03-24.t: Robert Koch Announces Discovery of the Tuberculosis Bacterium
03-24.s: German physician Robert Koch lectured before the Berlin Physiological Society, announcing he had isolated and grown the bacterium causing tuberculosis.

03-24.t: Birth of Reproductive Medicine Pioneer John Rock
03-24.s: American obstetrician and gynecologist John Charles Rock, who played a major role in developing the first birth control pill and pioneered IVF, was born.

03-25.t: Birth of Meningitis Vaccine Co-Discoverer James G. Zimmerly
03-25.s: American emergency physician James Gregory Zimmerly was born; he co-discovered a meningitis vaccine in 1970 while at Walter Reed Army Medical Center.
To curb local and community transmission of SARS-CoV-2, the Government of India implemented a complete nationwide 21-day lockdown, one of the largest pandemic containment measures in history.

03-26.t: Jonas Salk Announces Successful Polio Vaccine Trial
03-26.s: Dr. Jonas Salk announced from the University of Pittsburgh that his new inactivated polio vaccine had tested successfully on the first 90 patients.

03-27.s: The first successful non-direct blood transfusion was performed, advancing transfusion medicine beyond direct donor-to-recipient vascular connection.

03-27.t: FDA Approves Viagra for Erectile Dysfunction
03-27.s: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Viagra (sildenafil) as the first oral pill to treat erectile dysfunction in the United States.

03-27.t: WHO Officially Certifies India as Polio-Free
03-27.s: The World Health Organization officially certified India, along with ten other countries in the WHO South-East Asia Region, as polio-free, marking a historic triumph of the Universal Immunization Programme and Pulse Polio campaign.

03-28.s: Belgian physiologist Corneille Heymans was born; he won the 1938 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for demonstrating how the body senses blood pressure and oxygen levels.

03-29.t: Birth of Medical Geneticist Clarke Fraser
03-29.s: Canadian medical geneticist Clarke Fraser, known for bridging medicine and genetics and advancing genetic counseling, was born.
English pharmacologist John Vane was born; he contributed to understanding how aspirin relieves pain and reduces inflammation through prostaglandin inhibition.

03-30.t: First Use of Ether General Anesthesia in Surgery
03-30.s: In Jefferson, Georgia, Dr. Crawford Long used ether to anesthetize patient James Venable and painlessly excised a neck tumor, an anniversary now marked as National Doctors' Day.

03-31.t: Birth of Dr. Anandi Gopal Joshi
03-31.s: Anandi Gopal Joshi (born Yamuna Joshi) was born in Kalyan, Maharashtra. Overcoming severe societal barriers, she became the first Indian woman to obtain a degree in Western medicine in 1886.

03-31.t: Birth of Dr. T. S. Kanaka, Asia's First Female Neurosurgeon
03-31.s: Thanjavur Santhanakrishna Kanaka was born in Chennai. She became Asia's first female neurosurgeon and pioneered stereotactic neurosurgery and chronic electrode implantation in India.

03-31.t: Death of Insulin Co-Discoverer Charles Herbert Best
03-31.s: American-Canadian medical scientist Charles Herbert Best, who co-discovered insulin with Frederick Banting and researched heparin and choline, died on this day.
